evidence: Both gate dimensions carry real hard gates with all_pass aggregation and binary criteria, and scoring.toml lines 1-3 hold render=0.0 and constraints=0.0. test.sh lines 213-227 run the gates suite and score.py before the scored suite. Render gate (gates/render/judge.toml lines 25-33) covers reachability against a blank page, static mock, generic error or fatal browser error. It also has the auth legs: nothing private before sign-in, wrong password rejected, gwen opens her matters and messages. Constraints gate (gates/constraints/judge.toml lines 25-37) is the server-backing leg. Gwen posts 'Gate check JUDGE-G1' in M-11, it persists after reload, and harriet sees it in a separate browser context; 'a message that never saves, or that only the posting browser can see, fails this gate'. That excludes localStorage/static-shell facades as REVIEW_POLICY requires, and app_context.md line 24 makes the separate context feasible. All three scored prompts restate the in-dimension gate verbatim (functional prompt.md lines 11-19, polish lines 10-18, visual lines 18-26). The gate covers load without fatal error, gwen sign-in to protected content 'appropriate to the current state', and blank/empty/static mock/static shell/missing backend/facade failing, and 'If the gate fails, assign 0 to every criterion in this dimension'. Polish and visual say the gate is 'the only all-or-nothing rule', so the gate does not give partial credit. No same-origin requirement appears anywhere. Every gate and scored prompt explicitly allows external font/script/CDN requests (render lines 12-13, constraints prompt 13-14 and criterion line 29-30). The only 'origin' text is the functional replay method ('in-page calls from the app's origin'), not a gate condition. grep for same/cross-origin in task finds only the golden's fetch credentials option. Compared with the template, the task strengthens the gates (template constraints gate has no persistence/cross-account leg; template scored gates lack facade wording). Gwen remains eligible after the functional writes because no criterion walls a client, so the per-criterion functional gate stays satisfiable. Runtime: raw-evidence-index hashes all verify. Hosted runs on PREVIOUS v2 bytes gave Oracle render=1/constraints=1, GPT-5.6 render=1/constraints=1 and nop all 0. git diff da0bfd0f..HEAD shows tests/gates unchanged and the scored gate paragraphs unchanged since v2. Scripted golden on v3 source covers gate_constraints (functional.cjs line 117). Risk=true only because no configured judge run of the gates exists on these v3 bytes: the render gate has no v3 scripted or judge evidence, and the golden source changed after v2. Minor wording notes, not defects: 'seeded-looking facade' could make a weak judge suspicious of legitimate seed content, but it is qualified by 'real task data backed by the running local server'. A conforming app that keeps its session token only in JS memory would sign out on the constraints-gate reload, and the gate does not say to sign back in. Neither is a demonstrated counterexample. Broken-app probe: a localStorage SPA fails the separate-context leg. An in-memory server passes the gates but loses the functional persistence/restart criterion. That is the appropriate place for it, and the functional floor applies.
